newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses off to bad start on rates worry.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses off to bad start on rates worry.

text.p: European stocks made a poor start to the week on Monday as uncertainty over interest rates outweighed optimism engendered by Wall Street's third consecutive record close on Friday.
On currency markets, the dollar, which fell last week, was weaker by mid-morning with traders predicting little in U.S. economic data due this week to ignite a take-off.

In London, Europe's biggest bourse, shares slipped 0.2 percent. Traders said the market, already well below October's record levels, could come under more pressure from worries about rising interest rates.
"London is painting itself into a corner with these worries about domestic interest rates," said one.

Investors, already unsettled by a surprise quarter-point rate rise earlier this month, were further rattled by a Bank of England warning last week that inflation could breach the government's official target.
But the stocks recovered some of the early losses after British producer input prices, which rose 0.5 percent in October, showed, according to analysts, little underlying inflation pressure.
The FTSE 100 climbed after briefly dipping below the 3,900 level on the release of the producer price report which looked stronger than expected at first glance.
Some analysts said the jitters over interest rates and inflation were overdone. They saw the market mood improving once it was clear that 1997 would offer better growth with continued low inflation.
"The rating on the market is not terribly demanding and I don't see the need to be so worried," one trader said. "Not all interest rate increases are bad for equities."
In Frankfurt, stocks were down 0.3 percent, not drawing much comfort from the Dow Jones industrial average which closed at 6,219.82 points on Friday, the third peak in as many days.
The Dax index, which itself closed at a record high of 2,739.83 on Friday, slipped in thin trading, with the weaker dollar depressing the market.
The Paris bourse was closed for a national holiday commemorating the end of World War One.
The dollar drifted further against the yen as currency traders awaited Japanese indicators due on Tuesday but the U.S currency recovered some composure against the mark.
"The yen is likely to continue to push upwards ahead of the machinery orders data out tomorrow and the EPA's (Economic Planning Agency) report," said Julian Fisher, economist at Daiwa Europe.
"If both point to a continued economic recovery and one which is stronger than expected, it will fuel expectations that interest rate policy may be changed," he added.

Many dealers were also looking to the rate-setting meeting of the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Wednesday and U.S. retail sales and consumer prices on Thursday for clues on the health of the American economy.

"We expect the (U.S.) economic data to undershoot and there is near universal agreement that the FOMC is not going to raise rates," said Klaus Baader, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5050 marks and 111.27 yen, compared with 1.5045 marks and 111.60 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 6.5 points lower at 3,904.3.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 10.42 points at at 2,729.41.
The Paris bourse was closed for the day.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $379.75, versus $378.95 at the London close on Friday. Silver was at $4.85, up four cents.
